title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Twelve defects in the places never searched
summary: Six families that had never been audited were searched at once, each finding handed to a separate reader whose job was to refute it. Nine survived, and a sweep over every declaration of a real project found two more.

highlights.title: Cuts that stopped inside the declaration
highlights.description: A supertype list holding a `+` or an `=` collapsed the span to the header line. An expression body carrying on past `} else {` lost the rest. A cut could stop inside a raw string. Twenty three JSON fixtures on a real project were in that last case.

highlights.title: A dead enum entry takes its annotations
highlights.description: A leading annotation binds to the declaration that follows, so a deleted `@Deprecated OLD,` moved its deprecation onto the live sibling. On a last entry with a trailing comma, the file stopped parsing outright.

highlights.title: A stale corpus deleted live resource keys
highlights.description: Resource files never invalidated the corpus, and invalidating it during a scan was undone by that scan. Either way the pre change corpus was served for a minute, and the deletion followed the wrong verdict.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Three ways for a removal to stop inside the declaration it is cutting: a supertype list with a `+` or an `=`, an expression body continuing past its closing brace, and a raw string.
A dead enum entry now leaves with its own annotations, which otherwise moved onto the live entry below or broke the parse.
A resource key referenced through a member call, and every key of a module whose package ends in `android`, are no longer reported unused.
Resource, gradle and toml changes invalidate the corpus, and an invalidation during a scan is no longer undone by it.

Remove All Unreferenced Symbols and Remove Unused Resource Keys ask once instead of once per file, and the fix for a starved `@Subscribe` handler is offered in the shape handlers are actually written in.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: Every finding was handed to a separate reader whose job was to refute it, from scratch. Nine survived out of fourteen reported.
Two more came from sweeping the removal rule over all 8370 top level declarations of a real project rather than only the 501 currently reported dead.
